text:
maya: Quick alignment thread: we need to pick a ship strategy for customer-managed networking in the Private distro. Field asks are focused on upgrade safety, IP/peering preservation, and clear rollback behavior.

jordan: I'm available to lead the upgrade-playbook work. Major constraints: no database migrations that block rollback, minimal agent churn, and reproducible test scenarios.

sylvia: Field top asks summary: 1) keep customer-assigned IPs through upgrades 2) maintenance window guidance (exact steps + timing) 3) an operator-friendly rollback. Customers prefer deterministic outcomes over magical zero-downtime.

maya: Proposed UX: an installer flag and an explicit opt-in for "net-preserve" so customer still consents to the higher-touch path. Example CLI: 
```
./install --mode private --net-preserve on --ip-policy preserve
```

alejandro: From the agent side: we can preserve host/tenant IPs by avoiding veth/interface deletion during upgrade and pinning MACs. Pragmatic cost: ~1 engineer-week to prototype; plus QA for edge cases.

jordan: We'll need automated integration tests that cycle an agent and ensure IPs and BGP adjacency remain intact. Suggested matrix: small (10 tenants), medium (100 tenants), failover (simulated NIC bounce).

devx: Docs and DX asks: add a preflight checklist for NetOps (required routes, expected BGP sessions, ACLs) and a validation command, e.g., `redwoodctl network check --expected-peer <asn>` to confirm topology before upgrade. Include clear human steps for operator consent.

maya: Launch gates proposal:
- Gate A: Installer flag implemented + unit tests + basic integration test
- Gate B: Field pilots (2 customers) run at least one maintenance window each with our runbook
- Gate C: Public docs, rollback runbook, and a communications template for customer SREs

sylvia: Field can run two pilots but needs a sanitized checklist per customer and an escalation path. Also request a fallback: if preservation fails, provide an explicit switch to route traffic via our regional relay so customer uptime is preserved.

alejandro: Relay fallback design: lightweight egress proxy that forwards outbound L7 traffic to Redwood-hosted endpoints. Fast prototype in ~5 days; production-hardening ~2 weeks. Major caveat: requires customer's outbound bandwidth consent and potential billing discussion.

jordan: Tradeoffs: full IP preservation is safest for customer topology but increases upgrade manual steps and slows rollout. Alternative: preserve control-plane IPs (keeper BGP adjacencies) and rotate ephemeral data-plane addresses. That reduces operational burden but is not transparent to all customers.

maya: Decision to make: ship v1 with full IP preservation (higher ops) or control-plane-only (faster, lower-touch). Please comment with preference by EOD?

devx: Recommend control-plane-only for GA. Offer full IP-preserve as a labeled preview feature for high-touch customers with SRE engagement. This allows faster onboarding and fewer blockers for general customers.

sylvia: Field concurs. We'll mark a set of customers for preview. Need a comms template to surface expected operator involvement.

alejandro: I'll produce an agent skip-teardown patch and a relay prototype. ETA: prototype 5 workdays, hardened change 10 workdays.

jordan: I'll produce the integration test suite and upgrade-playbook doc. Will include a test matrix comparing ip-preserve vs control-plane-only.

maya: Actions: @alejandro prototype + agent plan, @jordan tests + playbook, @devx quickstart + validation command, @sylvia schedule pilots and prepare checklists, ops-bot create rollout ticket. Reconvene in 48h for firm dates.

ops-bot: Created PRIVNET-4123: "Private distro networking preserve rollout checklist" assigned to maya. Link: https://redwood.internal/PRIVNET-4123

maya: Thanks all. We'll lock on control-plane-only as the default for GA and open a preview track for full IP preservation. :rocket:
